claims.head: Who drives the play: the Wild
claims.body: The Wild have been near the top of the league at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Blackhawks one of the worst. Expect the Wild to spend more of the night in the Blackhawks’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

notes.text: Quinn Hughes is on injured reserve (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 4 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Brock Faber has taken his spot beside Jonas Brodin. That pair has had 52% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 67:11 together, about what it had with Hughes (56%).

Olli Määttä is out (upper body injury) and has missed the last 6 games. Brock Faber has taken his spot beside Jonas Brodin. That pair has had 48% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 90:20 together, about what it had with Määttä (48%).
Marcus Foligno is no longer killing penalties: 4% of the team’s shorthanded time in 14 games, down from 34% last season.
Danila Yurov has started killing penalties: on the ice for 26% of the team’s shorthanded time in 28 games, up from 6% last season.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 31% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 9th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 38%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Tyler Bertuzzi is out (illness) and has missed the last 2 games. He is a top-six forward.
Patrick Kane is on injured reserve (lower body injury) and missed their last game. He is a top-six forward. Teuvo Teräväinen has taken his spot beside Frank Nazar and Oliver Moore.

Bowen Byram is on injured reserve (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 19 games. He is a top-pair defenseman. Ian Cole has taken his spot beside Artyom Levshunov. That pair has had 33% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 79:38 together, down from 47% with Byram.
Wyatt Kaiser is suspended and has missed the last 3 games. Ian Cole has taken his spot beside Artyom Levshunov.
Luke Glendening joined from NYR on Nov 23 and has played beside Jordan Greenway and Cole Smith.

stakes: The Blackhawks go in eighth in the Central with 22 points, 20 points behind the Wild, first in the NHL.

CHI.head: The Blackhawks have a hill to climb
CHI.body: Even though Chicago has home-ice advantage and Minnesota will be without Hughes, the Wild have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Blackhawks can pull it off if they keep dangerous shots away.

MIN.head: The Wild have a lot going for them
MIN.body: Even though Chicago has home-ice advantage and Minnesota will be without Hughes, the Wild have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Blackhawks’ way back in is keeping dangerous shots away.

story.head: The Blackhawks are rolling
paras: The Blackhawks have won four straight, while the Wild (18-4-6) lost 4-3 in a shootout to Colorado on Friday. Going in, the Wild are first in the NHL and the Blackhawks last in the Central (tied for 27th in the NHL).
The Wild’s record (.750) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.633), largely thanks to their goaltending. The Blackhawks’ record (.423) is about what their chances are worth.

The Wild block more shots than almost anyone (2nd) and draw more penalties than they take (2nd), but get pinned in their own end on long shifts (32nd). The Blackhawks, by contrast, don’t block many shots (31st). Minnesota has allowed 2.29 goals a game, the second fewest in the league. The Hawks get their shots through better than almost anyone (2nd), but have struggled on the power play (31st). Chicago has allowed 3.73 goals a game, the third most in the league. The Wild are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Blackhawks. Beyond that, the Wild get in close, but the Blackhawks mostly shoot from distance.

Kirill Kaprizov (19 G / 30 A / 49 P in 28 GP) leads the Wild in scoring and is second in the NHL, with nine points in his last five games. For the Blackhawks, Roman Kantserov (15 G / 5 A / 20 P in 26 GP) leads the way in scoring, with eight points in his last five games. Sam Rinzel (2 G / 16 A / 18 P in 25 GP) is next in line.
Jesper Wallstedt (16-3-5 / .918 SV% in 24 GS) has been a rock in net for Minnesota and will likely start. Spencer Knight (9-11-1 / .895 SV% in 21 GS) is in line to start for Chicago.

items.text: The Wild have been without Quinn Hughes and Olli Määttä for several games.
The Blackhawks are newly without Tyler Bertuzzi, Patrick Kane and Wyatt Kaiser, and have been without Bowen Byram since Oct 13.
Roman Kantserov has 14 goals on chances worth about 5.6 goals, well above what his finishing usually turns chances into. Runs like that tend to cool off.
Blake Coleman has scored in three straight games.
